key_insight: Organic photovoltaic performance depends primarily on CT–CS energy alignment, while triplet recycling determines whether efficient charge generation and low voltage loss can coexist.
engineering_relevance: The model suggests targeting LE–CT offsets of 0.15–0.20 eV, weakly exothermic CT–CS offsets of 0.05–0.075 eV, and CT–T offsets no greater than about 0.1 eV.
method: Couple singlet and triplet exciton kinetics with device drift–diffusion transport.
Solve state populations and reversible transitions self-consistently.
Evaluate energy offsets and triplet-transfer kinetics in transient and steady-state operation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproduction of triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends, but provides no quantitative agreement metrics.
watch_item: This is a physics-based model, not an AI method; the proposed design windows need validation across additional materials and operating conditions.
paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
